parts:
We are a new user of “unmarked”. We have repeated point count data for
45 sites. We are trying to model abundance as a function of habitat
covariates which change with time. The point count was done 28 times
and we have habitat data for each of those 28 occasions; the habitat
changes with each point count survey. There are two habitat
covariates; corn and disturbed habitat. We used them as observational
covariates as they change on each observation. We do not have any site
covariates in our model.
This is what we did to create an unmarked object
veg.umf<-unmarkedFramePCount(y=bald.eagle.y,
obsCovs=list(corn=habitat.corn,disturbed=habitat.disturbed))

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Modeling abundance as a function of obsCovs
parts:
Hi BK,

Thank you for clearly articulating your question.

In this model, lambda is the expected number of individuals in year 1. Abundance after year 1 is modeled as the sum of 2 random variables (recruits and survivors). So if you want to model abundance throughout time, you need to model lambda as a function of corn in year 1, and gamma and/or omega as a function of corn. In other words, in addition to supplying corn as a yearlySiteCov, you need to create a siteCov that has the corn data from the first year:

veg.umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(..., siteCovs = data.frame(corn1 = habitat$Corn.1))
fm1 <- pcountOpen(~corn1, ~corn, ~1, ~1, veg.umf) # note the two names corn1 and corn

HTH,

Richard

For my species (endangered American burying beetle), weather conditions affect detectability and I would like to include multiple years of data to train the model of the detection process (p) so that it represents a wider range of variation (i.e. inter-annual variation in weather as opposed to only intra-annual variation from the first year in the model).

Thanks,

On Friday, March 2, 2012 3:11:15 PM UTC-6, Richard Chandler wrote:
Hi BK,

Thank you for clearly articulating your question.

In this model, lambda is the expected number of individuals in year 1. Abundance after year 1 is modeled as the sum of 2 random variables (recruits and survivors). So if you want to model abundance throughout time, you need to model lambda as a function of corn in year 1, and gamma and/or omega as a function of corn. In other words, in addition to supplying corn as a yearlySiteCov, you need to create a siteCov that has the corn data from the first year:

veg.umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(..., siteCovs = data.frame(corn1 = habitat$Corn.1))
fm1 <- pcountOpen(~corn1, ~corn, ~1, ~1, veg.umf) # note the two names corn1 and corn

HTH,
Richard
